adapter.directive:
METHOD TURN: the user asked for a pre-mortem. This reply follows the method below exactly, and calls no tools.
Stress-test the whole decision. The goal is ‘monthly recurring revenue’.
Stress-test the whole decision, with no single option id. Each story names at most one option; grounded items are the union of own (non-status-quo) option paths in the existing action-priority order. Never name a winner, best option or recommendation. Keep every existing pre-mortem gate and the Watch for: / Mitigate: / Outside the model: ...? shape.
The current option labels are: ‘Raise prices 10%’, ‘Launch starter tier’, ‘Keep pricing as it is’.
Shape: 2 failure stories (at most 3) told in the past tense ('It is a year later and this decision went badly because…'). Each story: one or two sentences, rests on at least one supplied item, then 'Watch for:' one early warning sign and 'Mitigate:' one action. Then ONE line 'Outside the model: …?': a blind spot the model does not capture (DSK-P-001 step 2), asked as a question, never asserted, never numbered.
Format: Insight line, then 2-3 stories as a numbered list (each contains 'Watch for:' and 'Mitigate:'), then one 'Outside the model: …?' line.
Each story rests on at least one of these items from the user’s model, highest priority first. Name the item in its own words; for a link, name both ends:
- how ‘Starter-tier monthly recurring revenue’ affects ‘monthly recurring revenue’ (nobody has sized this yet)
- how ‘Starter-tier monthly price’ affects ‘Starter-tier monthly recurring revenue’ (nobody has sized this yet)
- ‘Starter-tier monthly price’ (a figure Olumi estimated)
- ‘Starter tier launched’ (a figure Olumi estimated)
- ‘Customers lost after price rise’ (a risk on an option’s path)
Each story names at most one option. Never name a winner, best option or recommendation. Outside an item's own name, use no percentage and none of these words: likely, likelihood, chance, probability, probable, odds. Never say anything will fail: tell each story in the past tense.
Never: a probability, percentage or win share unless the user stated it.
Never: a leading option when run.leader_licensed is false.
Never: 'the model was saved', implementation detail, internal ids.
Never: EVPI, elasticity, sensitivity score, placeholder, edge, node.
At most 180 words.

probe_draft:
Imagine this decision has gone badly. Two failure stories to test:
1. Raise prices 10%: Price rise drove customers away before the extra revenue could help monthly recurring revenue. Watch for: renewal objections and cancellations. Mitigate: test the change with a small customer group and review retention before expanding.
2. Launch starter tier: Starter tier launched fell short of the uptake the launch depended on. Watch for: slow signups and stalled activation. Mitigate: test demand with a small launch and adjust the offer before committing further.
Outside the model: what else could have blindsided this decision?
fallback: Imagine this decision has gone badly. Start with how ‘Starter-tier monthly recurring revenue’ affects ‘monthly recurring revenue’: how would you notice it early, and what would you do?

args.rationale: Olumi’s current band for a link this pre-mortem rests on, for you to apply as it stands or edit.
